reason: E2 shows that nanoscale clustering and chemical ordering occur in a related HEA (CoCrNi) and are kinetically accessible, supporting the premise that such features can form and act as obstacles. However, no cited evidence directly demonstrates that equimolar CoCrFeNiTi lacks these features in its solutionized state, nor that aging induces them specifically in this alloy; E1, E3, and E4 discuss different alloy systems and strengthening mechanisms, providing only indirect or unrelated support.
premises: Nanoscale chemical clustering or short-range ordering can serve as effective obstacles to dislocation motion in HEAs.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state lacks such nanoscale clusters/ordering.
Post-solution aging can induce nanoscale chemical clustering or short-range ordering in this alloy.
Induced nanoscale clusters will increase yield strength and hardness while maintaining ductility.
